4. Defendant No.7 Golam Hossain Khan by filing one written statement and defendant No.2 Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Tangail by filing another written statement contested the suit. After taking evidence and hearing the learned Munsif decreed the suit in respect of the prayers in clauses (a) (c) (d) (e) and (h). The learned Munsif, however, did not grant any relief in respect of the other prayers of the plaintiffs. 

 7. Mr. Khondkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the Opposite parties has taken me through the relevant papers on record, the plaint and the written statements in particular. The learned Advocate submits that the plan tiffs have challenged the orders of the Governmental authorities as malafide, illegal and without jurisdiction and has sought for declarations to that effect. It could not be argued that a suit seeking such declarations could not be maintained. The learned Advocate submits that the concept of a hat as defined in section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not so important as regards the place of sitting but more important as regards the assembly of persons either daily or on particular days in a week for the purposes of buying or selling of commodities. The learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs have been beneficiaries of the hat named and styled as "Salimabad Hat" from time immemorial and the Salimabad hat always used to sit on Tuesdays and Fridays in a week and though due to unavoidable reasons the hat had to be shifted from one place to another. It could not be argued that the plaintiffs had not any vested interest in the sitting of the huts on these traditional days. The learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs’ main prayer is that Salimabad hat is entitled to sit on Tuesday and Fridays in a week. 

 "Hat" or "Bazar" has been defined in section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as follows:- (12) "hat', or "bazar" means any place where persons assemble daily or on particular days in a week primarily for the purpose of buying or selling agricultural or horticultural produce, livestock, poultry, hides, skins, fish, eggs, milk, milk products or any other articles of food or drink or other necessaries of life, and includes all shops of such articles or manufactured articles within such place." 

 8. It appears that by a number of notifications dated the 2nd April. 1956 published in the Dacca Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 2nd, April, 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates, taluks tenures holdings and tenancies situated in several districts including the district of Mymensingh were acquired with effect from 14th April, 1956. There is no dispute that hats and bazars were non-retainable khas lands. On the publication of the notifications, all non-retainable khas lands including hats in khas possession of a landlord vested absolutely in the Government free from encumbrances under section 3(4) of the S.A. &T Act. It is admitted on all hands that on the relevant date the Salimabad hat at Tebaria and the Sa lima bad Gohatta at Salimabad were in khas possession of the landlord and so the Salimabad hat at Tebaria which the defendants call Tebaria Chandganj hat and the plaintiffs call Salimabad Chandganj bat and the Salimabad Gobatta vested in the Government free from encumbrances. It was held in the case of Kali Charon Das and others Vs. Tamiruddin alias Jamiruddin and others reported in 10 DLR 523 relied on by Mr. Syed Isbtiaq Ahmed that the easements and customary rights of way are encumbrance and have been wiped out on such vesting. I do not see any reason why the customary right as claimed by the plaintiffs in the instant suit of compulsorily having the hat days on Tuesdays and Fridays will not also be -an encumbrance within the meaning of section 3(2) referred to above and be wiped out. Therefore even if the plaintiffs had the alleged customary right by immemorial user, it was wiped out on the vesting of the bat in the government free from encumbrances. 

 10. The plaintiffs have been given four other declarations, namely, the declarations prayed for in clauses (c), (d), (e) and (h) In clause (c), it has been prayed that an order dated 8.3.77 passed 'by Mr. M A. Samad, Joint Secretary L.A. and L.R Division be declared illegal and of no legal effect. In that order the Joint Secretary confirmed the order of the local Administration fixing Wednesdays and Sundays for Salamibad hat Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed could not place before me any statute rules bye laws or regulations by which the officers of the Government in the exercise of their executive power were required to fix the days of sitting of hat vested in the Government and managed by it on certain days of the week and bad no powers to change the days to some other days. It the absence of any law, rules, etc. and in the absence of any right of any immemorial user, as already found, the order of Mr. M.A. Samad, Joint Secretary dated 8.3.77 could not be brought into question before the Civil Court. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed bas submitted that this order was mala fide and contrary to materials on record. I have gone through the order of Mr. Samad dated 8.3.77. It appears from that order that he did not accept the recommendation of closing down the Salimabad hat even though he was of the view that only logical thing that should follow was the forfeiture. He observed that "since Salimabad hat was being run under the management of the Government in spite of the order of forfeiture and confiscation and Government has leased out the same, he did not interfere in the matter." He, however, found that Salimabad bat was a new hat and Tebaria hat was an old hat and holding of the new hat on the same days on which the old hat also sits is seriously affecting the old hat. The order intrinsically shows that the Joint Secretary has .applied his judicial mind to the facts of the case and has made the impugned order and as such an order can hardly be called in question as mala fide and arbitrary Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed has further argued that the conclusion that Salimabad bat was older than Tebaria hat was against the materials on record. It appears that the Joint Secretary has confirmed the decision of the local Administration and the local Administration has taken the decision after having a local enquiry done and on the basis of report of the local enquiry. It could not be said that there was no basis for the conclusion arrived at by the Joint Secretary. The courts below have on evidence taken by them come to the conclusion that Salimabad hat was older than Tebaria hat. It did Dot fall within the domain of the Civil Court to make an independent enquiry as to which hat was older. The enquiry could only be directed to see whether the order or the Joint Secretary was malafide and arbitrary and whether on the materials before the Joint Secretary, this was so. The materials that were brought before the court in this regard were materials extraneous to such consideration. In the case of Province of East Pakistan Vs. Haji Muhammad Juman and another reported in PLD 1960 (Karachi), 908, it has been held that Civil Courts cannot sit in judgment over the decisions of the Revenue officers if they have acted in exercise of their jurisdiction, There is a sharp, if sometimes fine, distinction between jurisdiction and exercise of jurisdiction. Jurisdiction is the authority to hear and decide a question. It is sometimes exceeded in its exercise, but so long as a question is decided within the limits of a jurisdiction it is immaterial, from jurisdictional point of view, whether the decision is right or wrong. In the instant case it cannot be said that the Joint Secretary has acted in excess of his jurisdiction. It is not for the Civil Court to correct errors of Judgment of even the Revenue officers far less the executive officer in the exercise of purely Executive powers. I am, therefore, of the opinion that the decree declaring the order dated 8.3.77 passed by the Joint Secretary in terms of prayer clause (e) is illegal and erroneous on the face of the record. Prayer clause (d) in relation to an order dated 4.4.78 Ext. A(1). This is an order of Mr. S.H. Khan, Joint Secretary Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms. In this case also the Joint Secretary confirmed the fixation of the hat days of Salimabad on Wednesday and Sundays as 'being reasonable and rational', He has observed that 'the hat could also be closed down and. this has not been done and it has been allowed to function under the management of the Government. He states that the two hats are situated closely it is neither desirable nor justifiable that the two hats should sit on the same days. It is only natural that the two hats 'should sit on different days. He stated that 'since Tabaria hat has been sitting on Tuesdays and Fridays, there is no reason to change its days. Since Salimabad hat is a new hat and has been allowed to continue fixation of its hat days on Wednesdays and Sundays should remain. For the reasons stated in relation to the order dated 8.3.77 Ext. A. I hold and find that the order dated 4.4.78, Ext. A(l) was not also liable to be declared illegal, void and inoperative and not binding upon the Salimabad Hat. In terms of clause ‘e' a decreed was passed that a memo dated 24.2.78 issued by the Deputy Commissioner was illegal, without lawful authority, malafide, void, inoperative, not binding upon the Salimabad hat and is of no legal effect. In this order the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner directed the Sub-divisional Officer, Tangail to implement the forfeiture of Salimabad hat. It is admitted that the order of forfeiture or confiscation of Salimabad hat has not been acted upon and the orders of the Joint Secretaries earlier referred allowed the Salimabad hat to continue sitting in spite of that order. In this view of the matter, the plaintiffs cannot be said to have any cause of action in respect of the order 24.2 78 Ext. A(2), In prayer clause 'R' a relief was prayed for that a decree be declared that Tebaria hat is a new hat and is liable to be Closed down under the law wand there cannot be any compensation assessment roll in respect of Tebaria hat and it cannot be put in auction. The plaintiffs have not claimed any right whatsoever in relation to Tebaria hat, not even the right of beneficial enjoyment. The plaintiffs have evidently no cause of action to get the declaration in clause 'h'. Besides, as already stated, Tebaria hat at Tebaria I which the plaintiffs call Salimabad Chandgaon hat and the defendants call Tebaria Chandgaon hat has stood acquired by the Government by a notification of the 2nd April, 1956 referred to earlier and has vested in the Government. Evidently a compensation assessment roll must be prepared. There cannot be any question of not preparing C.A. Roll in respect of that hat. Tebaria hat has vested in the Government and plaintiffs cannot dictate the Government to close down the Tebaria hat and the declaration that Tebaria hat is a new hat is not also called for. In fact it has been found by the Executive Authorities as already noticed that the hat at Tebaria is older than the that at Salimabad. The prayer in clauses U.K. &L. have not been granted to the plaintiff and there was no appeal against the trial court's refusal of those prayers. Before I conclude, 1 would like to observe that the learned Additional Judge in his judgment has observed that "I agree that the authorities concerned may direct for changing the hat days of a particular hat considering its better management and considering the convenience' and inconvenience' of the local people"; But he was of the view that the decision of the Additional Deputy Commissioner. Tangail was against principle of natural justice and without objecting finding of fact. The materials on record not only do not justify such a view but also are against such a view. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed could not and, did not also attempt to justify the view taken by the learned Additional District Judge. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed argued that the orders of the executive authorities were arbitrary malafide and against materials on record and his grievance was that the courts below did not direct their attention to this aspect of the matter. 'This court has fully considered this aspect of the matter and has failed to concur with Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed that the impugned executive orders were malafide and arbitrary and were not based on materials or contrary to materials on record. They cannot be attacked on that score In view of the discussion above. I hold that the courts below have committed errors of law apparent on the faces of the record which vitiate their Judgment and call for an interference by this court.
